I am a woman of 46 years, farming here in the South South. I plant mostly cassava and some yam on this plot of less than one hectare near my house. I don't have much money for chemical fertilizer this season, and the soil here still gives reasonable yield, so I will depend on the small manure from my goats and chickens spread on the mounds. For cassava I always keep cuttings from last year's harvest — the local variety does well in our soil and I trust it. My children help me with weeding and harvesting, but I will need to hire a few young men for clearing and making the heaps because my back cannot do all that work alone.
